trials.name: BAN2401-G000-201
trials.primary_endpoint: Core Study Phase: Change From Baseline in Alzheimer's Disease Composite Score (ADCOMS) at Month 12
trials.results_summary: The trial failed to meet its primary Bayesian clinical endpoint at 12 months. However, secondary analyses at 18 months demonstrated significant dose-dependent reductions in brain amyloid and signals of clinical benefit, leading to the initiation of Phase 3.

trials.name: Clarity AD
trials.primary_endpoint: Core Study: Change from Baseline in the CDR-SB at 18 Months
trials.results_summary: Met the primary endpoint, reducing clinical decline on the CDR-SB by 27% compared to placebo at 18 months, alongside significant clearance of brain amyloid beta. These results successfully replicated the Phase 2b proof-of-concept findings and led to traditional FDA approval.

trials.name: AHEAD 3-45
trials.population: Participants With Preclinical Alzheimer's Disease and Elevated or Intermediate Amyloid
trials.primary_endpoint: Change From Baseline in Preclinical Alzheimer Cognitive Composite 5 (PACC5) Score and Amyloid PET SUVr at Week 216

trials.population: Subjects with Mild to Moderate Alzheimer's Disease
trials.primary_endpoint: Safety and Tolerability of Single Ascending Dose (SAD)
trials.results_summary: Demonstrated acceptable safety, tolerability, and pharmacodynamics for single and multiple ascending doses, establishing safety parameters that supported Phase 2 development.

related_evidence.description: Publication of the Phase 2b proof-of-concept trial analyzed in the document (BAN2401-G000-201).
Publication of the Phase 3 Clarity AD trial results showing lecanemab significantly slowed clinical decline.
FDA grants accelerated approval to Leqembi (lecanemab) based on biomarker endpoint (amyloid reduction) derived from the Phase 2b trial.
FDA grants traditional full approval to Leqembi (lecanemab) after the Phase 3 Clarity AD trial confirmed clinical benefit.

evidence_assessment: The clinical evidence supporting lecanemab is strong and fully replicated in later-stage trials. While the Phase 2b trial (NCT01767311) analyzed in the document missed its primary 12-month clinical endpoint and suffered from severe genetic imbalance due to mid-trial regulatory changes, its secondary 18-month findings of robust amyloid clearance and nominal clinical benefit proved to be highly predictive. The subsequent 1,906-patient Phase 3 Clarity AD trial (NCT03887455) successfully met its primary endpoint, demonstrating a 27% reduction in clinical decline on the CDR-SB at 18 months alongside significant amyloid reduction. This robust Phase 3 replication fully vindicates the proof-of-concept claims made in the Phase 2b paper and led directly to traditional FDA approval in July 2023.
discrepancies: The document reports a total sample size of 854 participants, whereas the ClinicalTrials.gov registry lists the final enrollment count as 856.

The document explicitly concludes that the Phase 2b study achieved 'proof-of-concept' based on secondary 18-month endpoints, whereas the registry confirms the singular pre-specified primary objective was the 12-month ADCOMS target, which the trial definitively failed.
